survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This country note is a descriptive OECD indicator profile rather than an analysis of student microdata from an ILSA (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIRLS). It reports system-level statistics (e.g., unemployment by educational attainment, expenditure per student, field-of-study shares) using OECD indicator tables referenced in the text, not a student-level modeling dataset. As a result, complex survey weights and replicate-weight procedures (e.g., BRR/jackknife) are not applicable to the note’s presented outputs. For users who consult the underlying Education at a Glance 2025 indicator tables, the appropriate weighting and variance estimation approach is documented in the corresponding Sources, Methodologies and Technical Notes and indicator-specific documentation.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values (PVs) are not applicable because this note does not analyze cognitive achievement outcomes from ILSA microdata (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIRLS PV-based test scores). Instead, it summarizes education-system indicators such as attainment distributions, unemployment rates by attainment, expenditure per student, and tertiary student mobility shares. Missing-data handling is not reported because the document is an indicator country note that points to OECD indicator tables and technical notes rather than providing an explicit statistical estimation pipeline with missingness procedures.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: This is a country note summarizing Education at a Glance 2025 indicators for South Africa using the latest available reference year(s) for each indicator. The note does not define an analytic student-level subsample (e.g., grade band, assessment module, or case exclusions); instead, it directs readers to the corresponding Education at a Glance 2025 tables and the Sources, Methodologies and Technical Notes for indicator-specific definitions and any data processing steps.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Education at a Glance 2025 country note for South Africa provides descriptive system-level indicators rather than an empirical student-level modeling study. It reports trends in unemployment among 25–34 year-olds by educational attainment (e.g., changes from 2019 to 2024), compares employment and wage patterns by attainment levels, and summarizes tertiary education participation indicators such as the share of international students and the distribution of graduates across broad fields of study. It also presents financial resource indicators, including government expenditure per full-time equivalent student by education level (with tertiary including R&D) and education investment as a share of GDP. The note does not specify an ILSA assessment cycle, grade, or PV-based achievement outcome, and it does not provide model performance metrics or an ML pipeline. Readers are referred to the Education at a Glance 2025 indicator tables and the OECD Sources, Methodologies and Technical Notes for the underlying data definitions and methodological details.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The document is not an ILSA microdata analysis and does not implement or evaluate machine learning models; therefore, fields such as PV handling, missing-data handling, sample sizes, and ML techniques are not populated in the way they would be for an empirical predictive paper. The note’s outputs are indicator summaries (e.g., unemployment rates, expenditure levels, attainment shares) drawn from OECD’s compiled datasets and published tables, with methodological details deferred to the referenced technical notes. Consequently, there is no student-level target variable, no predictive modeling design, and no reported performance metrics to extract into main_findings.
